title: Manassas Jazz Festival and ending her retirement
summary: In 1966 she sang a couple of songs at Manassas, Virginia, with Cliff Jackson, after years away because of raising her daughter.

blocks.x: Now we come to a long absence from the recording studio. In fact, eight years before you recorded again, in May of 1966.
Yeah.
At the Manassas Jazz Festival.
Yeah. Cliff had, you know, knew all these people. And this Johnson

And these were -- Johnson would -- Cliff knew these people from Virginia because they came into Ryan's all the time where he was working.
And I think that Cliff was trying to -- you know, say, 'Look, you might as well be singing.' you know.
So, the concert came up and I went down with him and --
How far away is Manassas from Washington, D. C.?

About 29 miles, or something like that. It's not too far. It's -- what do you call it, Dulles Airport. When you go down, you had to get out Dulles Airport and get the you drive from there into Manassas.
And -- so, Cliff was playing and he had -- They had Tommy Gwaltney's group down

there. Marion McPartland was down there, and all that. So, I said I would do the concert.
I went down and I sang a couple of selections. And this was my first time out, you know, during the time that I was supposed to be retired.
I went down there for the lark, you know what I mean?
Yes.
So --
Did you, in fact, do any other things like this which didn't find their way onto records?
Uh --
Was this a hard and fast period or good timing for you or...
Yeah, it was --
You just stopped performing.
I stopped, and I didn't bother about trying to do anything --
Toward the end of my retirement, I got, I guess through my affiliation with Cliff, I would go down to Ryan's and we would go to different places.

If somebody said, you know, sing, I would sing. But I wasn't singing professionally. I wasn't working at it.
So it was sort of hard for me -- it was hard for anybody to get me out, because I felt that you can't two things.

You know, I mean, if I was going to sing, I'd have to get out there and sing. And if I was going to do my other work -- I had to devote my time to that because I had a lot to learn. And it didn't bother me.
If I sang, I sang just for kicks. So, when this Manassas came up, I went down with Cliff and I sang these songs.
And the next thing I knew, they were out on an album. I didn't even know they were being recorded until a little later.
This performance took place in a high school auditorium.
That's right.
I don't even think -- although it was released, you say, in '66 -- it was probably was done

much earlier than that.
No, no. It's a '66 festival, and it probably didn't come out until later.
Yeah.
So I guess it was 1966 that I went down there.
And, of course, I would say that this was probably the beginning of my actually coming out of retirement.
Because as you know, the reason I stopped was because Paula, my daughter, was in elementary school, and I was trying to follow behind her to keep her on what I thought might've been the right track.
But she's getting older now and she doesn't need me anymore, and I had a little bit more time to, you know, spend on myself.
I was sort of on a fence there. I wasn't sure I wanted to do anything. But it's just like the ham, if you get a little encouragement, you'll keep on.
But I held out for quite a long time. I
